periods.title: Spring
periods.lead: A quiet season. The main find is morels right after the snow melts — and poisonous false morels grow right beside them.

periods.title: Early summer
periods.lead: The season gains momentum: first boletes, chanterelles and porcini appear after warm rains.

periods.title: Mid summer
periods.lead: Variety widens: saffron milkcaps and milkcaps join the main species. The first dangerous lookalikes appear — check the stem base carefully.

periods.title: Late summer
periods.lead: Peak season — and peak risk: death caps and destroying angels fruit now, easily confused with field mushrooms and parasols. Honey fungi begin.

periods.title: Early autumn
periods.lead: Prime time for honey fungi. Their deadly lookalikes must be known by heart (see the funeral bell).

periods.title: Late autumn
periods.lead: The season winds down: oyster mushrooms, blewits, late honey fungi remain. Many mushrooms turn soft and unusable after frosts.

periods.title: Winter
periods.lead: Almost nothing except oyster mushrooms in a thaw and velvet shank. Chaga and polypores can be found year-round.
